newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Germany's Rexrodt studies NZ labour contract model.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Rexrodt studies NZ labour contract model.

text.p: Germany should follow New Zealand's example in some areas of labour reform, particularly allowing free contracts between employee and employer, German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Monday.

"We extensively and intensively discussed the reform process in New Zealand and we are very impressed about the success and to some extent New Zealand is a model for Germany," Rexrodt told journalists after meeting New Zealand's ministers of trade, finance and commerce. Asked if Germany could go as far with reform of the labour market as New Zealand had, he said Germany had some of the reforms already in place.

"In other areas we have to go in the direction of New Zealand, especially free contracts between employees and employers, and frankly speaking in this area I don't expect for the next months such success as New Zealand had, because...our unions oppose strongly such deep reform.
"In most areas flexibility is well underway and I think we have a good chance to be the locomotive in this area within the European Union."

New Zealand freed up its labour market in 1991 with legislation which outlawed the promotion of multi-employer contracts by way of strike action and encouraged individual contracts and a flexible labour market.

"Especially, we can learn and orient our own reforms (to) what New Zealand has done in the labour market and in other areas like open(ing) up the market and the health system and so on," Rexrodt said.
"I think our reforms need a little bit longer because we are a relatively large country with some difficulties to overcome.
"But we are well underway and I think Germany will make it in the next years", he added.
